chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from he who mentioned him, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the divorced woman, does she perform Hajj during her waiting period? He said: If she is newly divorced (has not performed Hajj before), she performs Hajj during her waiting period. And if she has already performed Hajj, she does not perform Hajj until she completes her waiting period. And this indicates that there is no obedience due to the husband from her in the Hajj of Islam.

key_terms.صُرُورَة: Newly divorced (one who has not performed Hajj before)

ai.seo_question: Can a divorced woman perform Hajj during her waiting period (iddah)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar clarifies that a divorced woman’s obligation to perform Hajj is personal and independent of her husband’s consent, allowing her to undertake it during her 'iddah if she has not yet fulfilled it. The distinction between the 'surur' (one who has not performed Hajj) and the one who has already done so highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the timing of this pillar of Islam. This ruling underscores the autonomy of the woman in fulfilling her religious duties even while in a transitional marital state.
